text: Identification is weak and contradictory: uncalibrated scale, speed above video Nyquist, multimodal posterior. Reporting findings on that basis — no setpoint will be proposed from this capture.

title: Shaft speed not established — ambiguous posterior, above Nyquist
summary: Bayesian MAP is 1268.8 rpm (68% CI 1264.9–1270.7 rpm) but p_map=0.395 < 0.8, with competing modes 1134.1 rpm (p=0.318), 1796.0 rpm (p=0.146) and 5787.7 rpm (p=0.141); 17/18 peaks explained. This conflicts with the audio blade-pass track speed_hz_now=48.357 Hz = 2901.4 rpm. Video Nyquist is only 15.0 Hz at 30 fps (near_nyquist_warning), so either candidate shaft frequency (21.1 or 48.4 Hz) is above Nyquist. display_rpm is null — no independent check. A 2-pole induction-motor what-if returned the identical posterior (MAP 1268.8 rpm, p=0.395), so it does not resolve the ambiguity; reverted to centrifugal_pump. Do not use any of these speeds as fact. Required: tachometer/strobe or tach-pulse capture plus legible nameplate (poles, rated rpm, vane count).

title: Amplitudes uncalibrated — ISO 20816 zone not reportable
summary: scale_calibrated=false and overall iso_zone=null. Raw channel levels (s1 motor housing 217.6, s2 pump casing 219.7, s3 PVC pipe 387.5 mm/s RMS) are physically implausible / uncalibrated and must NOT be reported as ISO Zone D or absolute severity. Amplitudes are relative only: s3/s1 ratio ≈1.78, s3/s2 ≈1.76, i.e. PVC pipe motion relatively largest. Conclusions restricted to frequencies, orders, phase and ratios. Required: calibrated contact accelerometer capture with credible scale reference.

title: Imbalance, misalignment, bearing and flow faults not evaluable
summary: Fault posterior is at prior with evaluable:false for imbalance (P=0.15, prior 0.15), misalignment (P=0.10), blade/vane-pass flow (P=0.10), bearing (P=0.08) and rotor-bar (P=0.05) — no evidence in dB. Order amplitudes 1x/2x/3x are all 0.0 mm/s, which with shaft above the 15 Hz Nyquist is a failed track, not proof of absence. Therefore the 1x-radial imbalance rule and the 2x with ~180° phase-across-coupling misalignment rule cannot be applied. Required: tach-synchronised calibrated radial+axial vibration at motor and pump housings with cross-coupling phase, at a sampling rate well above 10x shaft.

title: Cavitation not supported — weak index, negative audio
summary: Cavitation index 0.381 (HF energy fraction 0.094, HF kurtosis 0.033) gives only +1.1 dB evidence: fault P=0.100 vs prior 0.08. Audio corroboration is negative — cavitation_like=false, no gravel-like crackle; sounds are electric motor hum/whine, water gush/flow, splash and pipe hiss, speed steady. Do not diagnose cavitation from this. If suspected, required: suction pressure / NPSHa, discharge pressure and flow, plus high-bandwidth impulsive-noise capture.

title: Looseness/resonance not supported; only low-frequency FDD structural modes
summary: Looseness P=0.006 (1–10x harmonics 0, −8.7 dB; half-order 2.7 dB, −4.3 dB) and resonance P=0.030 (critical speed in swept range 0, −6.5 dB); modes=[] and campbell_criticals=[] — no order-crossing/critical-speed evidence. FDD structural modes on motor housing/pump casing/PVC pipe: 2.8125 Hz (zeta 0.134, sv_ratio 87.8), 3.984 Hz (zeta 0.035, sv_ratio 69.9), 4.688 Hz (zeta 0.209, sv_ratio 122.0), 8.672 Hz (zeta 0.056, sv_ratio 265.4). No damping error bars are provided and the 20.9% damping at 4.688 Hz should be treated cautiously. With shaft speed unresolved and above Nyquist, no resonance conclusion is possible.

text:
## Assessment: inconclusive — do not optimise from this capture

**Asset:** Centrifugal pump, nameplate text “NUMATIC PUMPS”; poles, rated rpm, kW and vane count all unread/0.

### 1. Shaft speed is not established
- Bayesian MAP: **1268.8 rpm** (68% CI **1264.9–1270.7 rpm**), but **p_map = 0.395**, well below the 0.8 threshold.
- Competing modes: **1134.1 rpm (p=0.318)**, **1796.0 rpm (p=0.146)**, **5787.7 rpm (p=0.141)**; 17/18 peaks explained.
- This conflicts with the audio blade-pass track: **48.357 Hz = 2901.4 rpm**.
- Video Nyquist is only **15.0 Hz at 30 fps**, with near-Nyquist warning — both candidate shaft frequencies are above it, so aliasing cannot be excluded.
- `display_rpm` is null: no independent check or display error can be reported.
- A 2-pole induction-motor kinematic what-if returned the **identical posterior** (MAP 1268.8 rpm, p=0.395) and was reverted; it does not resolve the ambiguity.

### 2. Absolute vibration severity is not reportable
`scale_calibrated=false`, overall `iso_zone=null`. The raw levels — motor housing 217.6, pump casing 219.7, PVC pipe 387.5 mm/s RMS — are uncalibrated/relative only and must **not** be quoted as ISO 20816 Zone D. Relatively, PVC pipe motion is largest: ≈**1.78×** motor housing and ≈**1.76×** pump casing.

### 3. Fault findings
- **Not evaluable** (posterior = prior, `evaluable:false`): imbalance P=0.15, misalignment P=0.10, blade/vane-pass flow P=0.10, bearing P=0.08, rotor-bar P=0.05. Order amplitudes 1×/2×/3× are all 0.0 mm/s — a failed track above Nyquist, not evidence of absence. The 1×-radial imbalance rule and 2×/~180° cross-coupling misalignment rule cannot be applied.
- **Cavitation not supported:** index 0.381 (HF energy fraction 0.094, HF kurtosis 0.033), only +1.1 dB → P=0.100 vs prior 0.08. Audio: `cavitation_like=false`, no gravel-like crackle; motor hum, water flow/splash and pipe hiss only.
- **Looseness/resonance not supported:** looseness P=0.006 (−8.7 dB harmonics, −4.3 dB half-order); resonance P=0.030 (−6.5 dB, no critical in range). `modes=[]`, `campbell_criticals=[]`.
- FDD structural modes (motor housing / pump casing / PVC pipe): **2.8125 Hz** (ζ=13.4%, sv_ratio 87.8), **3.984 Hz** (ζ=3.5%, 69.9), **4.688 Hz** (ζ=20.9%, 122.0), **8.672 Hz** (ζ=5.6%, 265.4). No damping error bars were provided; treat the 20.9% value cautiously.

### 4. Optimisation deferred
No optimiser run and no setpoint proposed. Variable-speed capability is not established (audio speed steady, no VFD/display evidence), speed is ambiguous, amplitudes are uncalibrated, and there are no Campbell criticals — so resonance margin, duty, specific energy and NPSH cannot be quantified without inventing numbers.

**Required recapture before diagnosis/optimisation:** tachometer/strobe or once-per-rev tach pulse; legible nameplate (poles, rated rpm, kW, vane count); calibrated radial+axial accelerometers on motor and pump housings with cross-coupling phase, sampled well above 10× shaft; a run-up/coast-down or stepped-speed sweep for the Campbell diagram; suction/discharge pressure, flow and NPSHa; and confirmation of drive type and required flow/head duty.
